text:
maya: heads up — on staging a support user just saw quick-nav links from a different workspace after we flipped the canary back. screenshot + console id attached.
alex: yikes. can you repro reliably? what steps did they take?
maya: yes reproduced. fast switch org -> open quick nav -> clicked saved filter -> saw rows belonging to org B. happens ~1/5 tries during rapid rollbacks.
priyanka: probably a routing-affinity or delegated-scope miss. quick nav uses delegated lookup via /internal/nav?workspace_id= — double-checking header passthrough.
jordan: logs show X-Route-Affinity: org-123 then a proxied call to internal service that responds with cached nav for org-789. entry in proxy cache TTL is 30s.
lisa: is the cache keyed by workspace header + cookie? or just cookie?
maya: looks like a race: proxied request loses the workspace header on fast retries so cache key falls back to session cookie which can be stale if users switch orgs quickly.
priyanka: that matches the symptom. rollout change yesterday added aggressive header rewrite to short-circuit auth; might be the regression.
ops-bot: deploy 1767450000 (canary) -> rollback 1767501000 detected. Canary toggle 'quicknav-prefetch' was toggled during rollback.
alex: repro snippet:
```
# as user A
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer abc" -H "X-Workspace: org-A" https://console.internal/nav?prefetch=true
# quickly switch to user B context
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer abc" -H "X-Workspace: org-B" https://console.internal/nav?prefetch=true
```
priyanka: mitigation options: 1) make proxy cache key include X-Workspace explicitly, 2) strip persistent session fallback for prefetch endpoints, 3) add strict scope check in nav service: verify returned nav.workspace_id == incoming header else 403 and log.
jordan: prefer 3 + telemetry: emit nav_scope_mismatch metric sampled with workspace_ids hashed. then we can monitor incidence during rollouts.
lisa: UX-wise, we should also add a rollout guard: disable prefetch cache when canary flag flips to avoid cross-affinity mixing.
maya: agreed. also need immediate fix for staging to repro and confirm. priyanka can you take proxy & nav service changes? alex can you add a telemetry counter and dashboard panel for nav_scope_mismatch?
priyanka: taking. will open PR for cache key change + defensive check. aim for a small rollout behind flag.
alex: I'll add a grafana panel (team dashboard) and an alert if rate > 0.1% of nav calls.
jordan: note: also check internal SDK used by quicknav — it has an internal 'delegated-session' behavior that may reuse kv cache keys. might be separate followup.
maya: thanks — adding steps to incident doc and assigning oncall to monitor. tagging @security to confirm no PII leaked. :eyes:
priyanka: PR link coming in 15m. will include test that simulates rapid org switch and asserts no nav content crosses workspace boundary.
lisa: once PRs merge, let's canary for 30m and keep the rollback button handy. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident annotated: multi-tenant quicknav scope leak (staging) — severity: medium; incident_id: QNAV-2026-03-21-1
maya: closing loop later with postmortem and rollout checklist change so future prefetch flags require cache-key review.
